newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan share prices close lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan share prices close lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Late profit-taking swept Taiwan's share prices on Tuesday, killing a big morning push into record territory and handing the index a loss but not breaking brokers' bullishness about the market's immediate outlook.

The weighted index, which soared on Monday to a six-year high, was strongly higher for most of the session but ran into a flurry of late selling that sent it to 3.26 points or 0.05 percent lower to close at 7,251.04.
Turnover was a heavy T$115 billion, the highest since a surge to T$125.9 on December 3.
Tuesday's downturn put what brokers called a temporary halt to a January bull run of more than 400 points.
"Some investors got a bit scared and began to take some profits in sectors that already had risen a lot," said Eric Liu, an analyst for National Securities.

Liu said the setback was unlikely to reverse the overall uptrend because more investors, many with fat year-end bonuses in hand, are expected to enter the market ahead of the February 7 Chinese lunar new year.
"It's natural for the market to take a break after setting a record high. And a three-point loss is pretty small," Liu said.

The paper sector, which had surged by 2.37 percent on Monday to lead the record-setting session, lost 1.35 percent on Tuesday with Cheng Loong falling by T$0.60 to T$20.10 and Chung Hwa Pulp dropping T$0.70 to T$27.20.
But electronics, the market's longstanding leading sector, found firm support by clocking a 0.27 percent sectoral rise to defy the flurry of profit-taking.
Computer giant Mitac International gained T$1.10 to T$35.10 on an acquisition from U.S. computer distributor Merisel Inc.
Brokers expected the index to shrug off Tuesday's dip and regain momentum on Wednesday, forecasting a 7,240-7,300 range.
